## codegraph
# Codegraph — code intelligence over an indexed knowledge graph

Codegraph is a SQLite knowledge graph of every symbol, edge, and file in
the workspace — pre-computed structure you would otherwise re-derive by
reading files (cached intelligence: thousands of parse/trace decisions you
don't pay to re-reason each run). Reads are sub-millisecond; the index lags
writes by ~1s through the file watcher. Reach for it BEFORE *and* while
writing or editing code — not just for questions: one call returns the
verbatim source PLUS who calls it and what it affects, so you edit with the
blast radius in view. More accurate context, in far fewer tokens and
round-trips than reading files yourself.

## One tool: codegraph_explore — use it instead of reading files

There is a single tool, `codegraph_explore`, and it is Read-equivalent. It
takes either a natural-language question or a bag of symbol/file names and
returns the **verbatim, line-numbered source** of the relevant symbols
grouped by file — the same `<n>\t<line>` shape `Read` gives you, safe to
`Edit` from — PLUS the call path among them (including dynamic-dispatch hops
like callbacks, React re-render, and JSX children that grep can't follow) and
a blast-radius summary of what depends on them.

Whether you're answering "how does X work" or implementing a change (fixing a
bug, adding a feature), call `codegraph_explore` before you Read. ONE call
usually answers the whole question. Codegraph IS the pre-built search index —
so running your own grep + read loop, or delegating the lookup to a separate
file-reading sub-task/agent, repeats work codegraph already did and costs more
for the same answer. A direct codegraph answer is typically one to a few
calls; a grep/read exploration is dozens.

## How to query

- **Almost any question — "how does X work", architecture, a bug, "what/where is X", or surveying an area** → `codegraph_explore` with a natural-language question or the relevant names. ONE capped call returns the verbatim source grouped by file; most often the ONLY call y… [truncated]

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

Engine: Google CEL (`cel-go`) — internal/filter (parser/engine in `internal/filter/engine.go`, `internal/filter/parser.go`, dialect SQL emission in `internal/filter/render.go`)

Mechanism: The `Engine` (`internal/filter/engine.go:14`) uses a `cel.Env` to parse the CEL filter string into an AST, converts it into a dialect-agnostic `Condition` tree, and then a `renderer` (`internal/filter/render.go`) walks that tree emitting per-dialect SQL (a `WHERE` fragment plus bound args) by branching on `DialectName` — `DialectSQLite`, `DialectMySQL`, `DialectPostgres` — for things like timestamp accessors and string length, which the memo store then splices into its `ListMemos` query for the active driver.

26	// Schedule runner every 12 hours.
27	const runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12
28	
29	func (r *Runner) Run(ctx context.Context) {
30		ticker := time.NewTicker(runnerInterval)
31		defer ticker.Stop()
32	
33		for {
34			select {
35			case <-ticker.C:
36				r.RunOnce(ctx)
37			case <-ctx.Done():
38				return
39			}
40		}
41	}
42	
43	func (r *Runner) RunOnce(ctx context.Context) {
44		r.CheckAndPresign(ctx)
45	}
46	
47	func (r *Runner) CheckAndPresign(ctx context.Context) {
48		instanceStorageSetting, err := r.Store.GetInstanceStorageSetting(ctx)
49		if err != nil {
50			return
51		}
52	
53		s3StorageType := storepb.AttachmentStorageType_S3
54		// Limit attachments to a reasonable batch size
55		const batchSize = 100
56		offset := 0
57	
58		for {
59			limit := batchSize
60			attachments, err := r.Store.ListAttachments(ctx, &store.FindAttachment{
61				GetBlob:     false,
62				StorageType: &s3StorageType,
63				Limit:       &limit,
64				Offset:      &offset,
65			})
66			if err != nil {
67				slog.Error("Failed to list attachments for presigning", "error", err)
68				return
69			}
70	
71			// Break if no more attachments
72			if len(attachments) == 0 {
73				break
74			}
75	
76			// Process batch of attachments
77			presignCount := 0
78			for _, attachment := range attachments {
79				payload := cloneAttachmentPayload(attachment.Payload)
80				s3ObjectPayload := payload.GetS3Object()
81				if s3ObjectPayload == nil {
82					continue
83				}
84	
85				if s3ObjectPayload.LastPresignedTime != nil {
86					// Skip if the presigned URL is still valid for the next 4 days.
87					// The expiration time is set to 5 days.
88					if time.Now().Before(s3ObjectPayload.LastPresignedTime.AsTime().Add(4 * 24 * time.Hour)) {
89						continue
90					}
91				}
92	
93				s3Config := instanceStorageSetting.GetS3Config()
94				if s3ObjectPayload.S3Config != nil {
95					s3Config = s3ObjectPayload.S3Config
96				}
97				if s3Config == nil {
98					slog.Error("S3 config is not found")
99					continue
100				}
101	
102				s3Client, err := s3.NewClient(ctx, s3Config)
103				if err != nil {
104					slog.Error("Failed to create S3 client", "error", err)
105					continue
106				}
107	
108				presignURL, err := s3Client.PresignGetObject(ctx, s3ObjectPayload.Key)
109				if err != nil {
110					slog.Error("Failed to presign URL", "error", err, "attachmentID", attachment.ID)
111					continue
112				}
113	
114				s3ObjectPayload.S3Config = s3Config
115				s3ObjectPayload.LastPresignedTime = timestamppb.New(time.Now())
116				if err := r.Store.UpdateAttachment(ctx, &store.UpdateAttachment{
117					ID:        attachment.ID,
118					Reference: &presignURL,
119					Payload:   payload,
120				}); err != nil {
121					slog.Error("Failed to update attachment", "error", err, "attachmentID", attachment.ID)
122					continue
123				}
124				presignCount++
125			}
126	
127			slog.Info("Presigned batch of S3 attachments", "batchSize", len(attachments), "presigned", presignCount)
128	
129			// Move to next batch
130			offset += len(attachments)
131		}
132	}
133	
134	func cloneAttachmentPayload(payload *storepb.AttachmentPayload) *storepb.AttachmentPayload {
135		if payload == nil {
136			return nil
137		}
138		cloned, ok := proto.Clone(payload).(*storepb.AttachmentPayload)
139		if !ok {
140			return nil
141		}
142		return cloned
143	}

13	// for lack of valid credentials. Each transport maps it to its own status code
14	// (Connect: CodeUnauthenticated, gRPC-Gateway: HTTP 401).
15	var ErrUnauthenticated = errors.New("authentication required")

17	// Authorizer is the single source of truth for method-level access control.
18	//
19	// It authenticates a request from its Authorization header and decides whether the
20	// (possibly anonymous) caller may reach a given RPC procedure. The Connect
21	// interceptor and the gRPC-Gateway middleware share one Authorizer so both
22	// transports enforce identical rules.
23	//
24	// Role-based authorization (admin checks) stays in the service layer; this type
25	// governs only authentication and anonymous access.
26	type Authorizer struct {
27		authenticator *auth.Authenticator
28		store         *store.Store
29		profile       *profile.Profile
30	}
31	
32	// NewAuthorizer creates an Authorizer backed by the given store, token secret, and
33	// instance profile.
34	func NewAuthorizer(store *store.Store, secret string, profile *profile.Profile) *Authorizer {
35		return &Authorizer{
36			authenticator: auth.NewAuthenticator(store, secret),
37			store:         store,
38			profile:       profile,
39		}
40	}

42	// Authenticate resolves the caller from the Authorization header, returning nil for
43	// an anonymous request. It never enforces policy — pair it with CheckAccess.
44	func (a *Authorizer) Authenticate(ctx context.Context, authHeader string) *auth.AuthResult {
45		return a.authenticator.Authenticate(ctx, authHeader)
46	}
47	
48	// CheckAccess enforces method-level access policy for procedure given the
49	// authentication result (nil = anonymous). It returns nil when the request is
50	// permitted and ErrUnauthenticated otherwise.
51	//
52	// Policy:
53	//   - Authenticated caller (access token or PAT): always permitted here.
54	//   - Anonymous + protected method: denied.
55	//   - Anonymous + public method, open instance: permitted.
56	//   - Anonymous + public method, private instance (no InstanceURL): permitted only
57	//     for the auth-bootstrap set, plus CreateUser during first-run setup.
58	func (a *Authorizer) CheckAccess(ctx context.Context, procedure string, result *auth.AuthResult) error {
59		if result != nil {
60			return nil
61		}
62		if !IsPublicMethod(procedure) {
63			return ErrUnauthenticated
64		}
65		if a.profile.AllowAnonymous() || a.allowedOnPrivateInstance(ctx, procedure) {

content.text:
q29.
Interceptor path: web/src/connect.ts (`authInterceptor`, line 156, registered in the shared transport's `interceptors`)

Token kinds: short-lived JWT **access tokens** (sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, ~15 min), **refresh tokens** (HTTP-only cookie, exchanged via `AuthService.refreshToken` to mint new access tokens), and **personal access tokens** (also validated as Bearer tokens)

Backend package path: server/auth (`server/auth/authenticator.go` — `AuthenticateByAccessTokenV2`, `AuthenticateByRefreshToken`, `resolveBearer` for access/personal tokens)

The frontend `authInterceptor` attaches the stored access token as a Bearer header, proactively/reactively refreshes it (on expiry or 401) via `refreshAccessToken` → `AuthService.refreshToken` using the refresh-token cookie, and the backend `server/auth` package validates these tokens (wired into the API via `server/router/api/v1/authz.go`'s `Authenticate` and the Connect/gateway interceptors).

q30.
memo created: DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook (`memos.memo.created`)
memo updated: DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook (`memos.memo.updated`)
memo deleted: DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook (`memos.memo.deleted`)
comment created: DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook (`memos.memo.comment.created`)

Delivery convergence: all call `webhook.PostAsync` (the created/updated/deleted trio funnel through the shared `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` helper first) — `internal/webhook/webhook.go` (`PostAsync` → `Post`).

All four dispatch functions are defined in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`; each fetches the recipient's webhooks via `Store.GetUserWebhooks`, builds a `WebhookRequestPayload`, and hands it to `webhook.PostAsync` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go` for asynchronous, HMAC-signed HTTP delivery.
